info.title: QAuth Admin API
info.description: The admin API of QAuth (ADR-019 Decision 7), served on the internal admin listener only. Every operation needs a DPoP-bound admin token, sent as `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with a proof made with its key for this listener's base URL and the request's path, whose account holds a grant on the realm in the path; a security operation also needs an approval bound to it.

servers.description: The admin listener, at ADMIN_API_BASE_URL. A proof's `htu` is that URL followed by the request's path.

post.summary: File an approval for one request of a security operation

operation.description: The id of the security operation the approval is for.

params.description: The operation's path parameters but `realmId`, which is the realm of the approval's path.

query.description: The operation's query, as its URL carries it.

body.description: The operation's body, as it will be sent.

reason.description: Why the requester asks. An approver sees it as quoted text, never as the operation.

schema.description: The request of a security operation an approval is filed for.

requestBody.description: The request of a security operation an approval is filed for.

201.description: An approval request for one request of a security operation, as filed, with what the two-admin rule makes of it.

approvalUrl.description: The approval page, on the requester's realm: `/approvals/{realmId}/{approvalId}` under its issuer, `realmId` naming the realm the approval acts on.

display.description: The operation as an approver sees it, rendered from the request when the approval was filed and stored then: typed display data, never HTML. Null once the approval is used, cancelled, denied or expired. The reason, params and query beside it are raw: show this instead.

twoAdmin.description: Whether a second admin's approval is recommended, as for every security operation, or mandatory, where the realm requires it for this request (`admin.twoAdminMandatoryOperations`). `approvalsRequired` is 2 exactly when it is mandatory.

eligibleApprovers.description: How many admins other than the requester could give a second approval now: those with a live grant holding approvals.approve on the realm made before the request, none created, granted a role or changed in the last 7 days. It counts the grants the caller’s realm sees: for a caller of another realm than the operator realm, none on every realm. Zero is the admin console’s cue for its single-admin warning.

post.summary: Seal a value for a security operation's secret member in the realm
post.description: Encrypts the value with the realm's data_at_rest key, bound to the operation, the member and the path parameters of the request it is for, and answers the ciphertext. It changes nothing and records no value; the operation's request carries the sealed value, never the secret, so its approval holds none.

operation.description: The security operation whose request will carry the value, such as `plugins.update`.

member.description: The secret member of that operation's body the value is for, as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901), such as `/secrets/clientSecret`: one the operation declares secret.

params.description: The path parameters of the operation's request the value is for, but realmId, such as `{ "plugin": "corp-sso" }`: the value opens only in a request with the same ones. None when the operation's path names only the realm.

value.description: The secret. Write-only: no response, row or log holds it.

schema.description: A value to seal for a security operation's secret member.

requestBody.description: A value to seal for a security operation's secret member.

sealed.description: The value, encrypted for this member of this operation in this realm: what the operation's request sends at the member, as { "sealed": … }.

get.summary: Read a realm and its policies
get.description: The ETag is the version of the realm's policies: a policy patch names it in If-Match.

patch.description: A JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) of the policies, judged on the merged document: a change a field’s annotation makes a security change needs realms.policies.security and an approval, any other realms.policies.write. If-Match names the ETag of the realm (428 without it, 412 when the policies moved). A secret field takes a value secrets.seal sealed for this operation and its member, or null to clear it.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

post.summary: Preview a change of a realm's policies
post.description: Takes the JSON Merge Patch realms.policies.update takes and answers what it would change and need, without saving it: each changed field before and after, tightening, loosening or neutral, its class, effects, permissions and scopes; for the whole patch, its class and scopes, whether it needs an approval, whether a second admin is recommended or mandatory, how many other admins could approve it, and the realm’s current ETag, which the save names in If-Match. It is judged by the same diff and classification as the save, and refused as the save is before it writes (400, 415, 422, and 503 while a later release’s policies are stored), the policy rules included; a sealed value is taken as setting its secret, unopened, so a value that does not open, and the sandbox ceiling the database checks, are refused by the save alone. It writes nothing, needs only realms.read, and shows a secret field only as set or not set. eligibleApprovers counts the other admins a second admin’s approval could come from: those with a grant on the realm, and, for a caller of the operator realm, those with a grant on every realm.

get.summary: List the installed AuthMethod plugins and the realm's state of each

name.description: The plugin's AuthMethod id: the name this API and its path give it.

type.description: The method's type: its sign-in routes answer under `/upstream/{type}` on the realm host.

package.description: The npm package the deployment loaded it from.

contract.description: The AuthMethod contract version it is written against.

enabled.description: The realm offers it. Always `false` while `mismatch` is set, whatever the stored state says.

config.description: The realm's config of the plugin: its plain members, never a secret one. While `mismatch` is set, the members the state another plugin wrote holds; a configure replaces them.

secrets.description: Each secret member of the plugin's config, by path, and whether it holds a value. Its value is never shown. While `mismatch` is set, none holds one: a secret sealed for another package or type never opens for this plugin.

package.description: The npm package of the plugin that wrote it.

type.description: The AuthMethod type it was written under.

configuredBy.description: The plugin the realm's state was written for. `null` before it was first written, or for a state written before QAuth recorded it.

mismatch.description: Why the realm's state is not this plugin's, or `null` when it is: `package_unrecorded` (written before QAuth recorded which package wrote it), `package_changed` (another package wrote it under this name), `type_changed` (this package wrote it under another type). Such a state is off and holds none of this plugin's secrets until a configure writes it again for this plugin, sealing its secrets again, and an enable is approved.

post.summary: Import a provider-issued private key as an AuthMethod plugin's client-assertion key
post.description: Imports a private key the provider issued, such as Sign in with Apple's .p8 key, with the provider's key id as its kid, as the key the signer signs the plugin's client assertions with in the realm. The key is sent sealed under privateKey, with a value secrets.seal sealed for plugins.keys.import, the member /privateKey and the params { plugin }; it is stored sealed under the KEK and never returned. Its algorithm must be the one the realm's configuration of the plugin asks for, so the plugin is configured first: 409 when its configuration names no client assertion. The plugin's first key of the algorithm signs at once; a second waits as next until plugins.keys.activate, and 409 while one is already waiting or the kid is taken. 400 for a key that is not an unencrypted private key of the algorithm.

parameters.name: plugin
parameters.description: The plugin's name: its AuthMethod id, such as `corp-sso`.

post.summary: Switch an AuthMethod plugin's client assertions to its next key
post.description: Makes the plugin's next key the one the signer signs its client assertions with in the realm, and retires the key that signed until then. The switch runs once approved, with no pre-publication window, since the provider already holds the key's public half. Refused with 409 when the kid names no next key of the plugin.

parameters.name: plugin
parameters.description: The plugin's name: its AuthMethod id, such as `corp-sso`.

post.summary: Verify an account as the operator
post.description: Records the operator's verification on the account: it counts as verified beside its primary identity, for signing in where verified accounts are required and for owning an agent, and an unclaimed account is claimed, so another person's later mailbox proof no longer ends it. email_verified is not changed. A security operation: it needs users.security and an approval, filed with approvals.create against the account as it stands. Its body is an empty object. 404 for an account the realm does not hold, 409 for a disabled account or one an operator already verified. An approval filed against the account as it stood no longer matches once a credential is added, removed or proved: the call is answered 403 approval_required, and 412 when the account changes during the call.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the account, or * for its current state: the approval binds the account's state it was filed against either way.

delete.description: Deletes the account at once, with its credentials, recovery codes, consents, attributes, upstream identities, refresh tokens and codes. Every session it holds ends first, browser and logout-only alike, and each client a session signed in to with a back-channel logout URI is queued a logout token in the same transaction; its access tokens no longer introspect. A security operation: it needs users.delete and an approval, filed with approvals.create against the account as it stands. The one exception is a service account that holds the built-in role account-closer on exactly this realm, through a client the operator made: it deletes with no approval while the realm needs one for the deletion, and names none; where the realm's admin.twoAdminMandatoryOperations lists users.delete, it needs the approvals as anyone does. Idempotent by id: an id the realm does not hold, whether unknown, deleted already or another realm's account, is answered as a deletion is, 204, and changes nothing and records no event, so a retry with If-Match: * answers as the first call did, with an approval of its own (an approval is used once) or, for such a service account, with none. A service account's account, and an account that holds an admin grant, are refused with 409. An approval filed against the account as it stood no longer matches once a credential is added, removed or proved: the call is answered 403 approval_required, and 412 when the account changes during the call.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the account, or * for its state as it is: the approval binds the account's state it was filed against either way. A retry sends *: one that names the account's ETag answers 412 once the account is gone.

204.description: The account is deleted, or the realm holds no account with this id: the answer is the same.

get.summary: List the clients of a realm
get.description: Every client of the realm, whoever owns it (a developer, an operator, the client itself), newest first, one page at a time. q keeps the clients whose client_id or name holds it. The developer API's list, of a developer's own clients only, is not this one.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Only the clients whose client_id or name holds this text, case ignored; % and _ match themselves.

post.description: Registers a client no developer owns, provisioned by the operator: the server generates its id and client_id, and for client_secret_basic and client_secret_post its secret, which this answer carries once. A security operation: it needs clients.security and an approval, filed with approvals.create for this body. The checks of every registration path apply, the first-party rules (ADR-017 Decision 2) and the client token lifetimes too (422 naming each field).

get.description: The ETag is the version of the client: an update, a deletion and lifting a suspension name it in If-Match.

patch.description: A JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) of the client, judged on the patched client field by field, as the client field table says: changing the redirect URIs, the post-logout redirect URIs, the authentication method or keys, first-party trust, the verified domain or the agent fields, adding a grant type or a qauth: scope, setting a back-channel logout URI, widening the client_credentials scopes, switching PKCE or DPoP off, a laxer environment and a longer token lifetime need clients.security and an approval; every other change clients.write. A client's token lifetime is never longer than the realm's (422). If-Match names the ETag of the client (428 without it, 412 when it moved). A CIMD client is read-only: 409, naming its document.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

delete.description: Deletes the client with its authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents and API keys. A security operation: it needs clients.security and an approval, filed against the client as it stands; If-Match names its ETag (428 without it, 412 when it moved). A CIMD client is read-only: 409, naming its document. A service account's client is not deleted: 409; disable the service account instead.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

post.summary: Preview a change of a client
post.description: Takes the JSON Merge Patch clients.update takes and answers what it would change and need, without saving it: each changed field before and after, tightening, loosening or neutral, its class, effects, permissions and scopes; for the whole patch, its class and scopes, whether it needs an approval, whether a second admin is recommended or mandatory, how many other admins could approve it, and the client’s current ETag, which the save names in If-Match. It is judged by the same field table and refused as the save is (400, 415, 422; 409 for a CIMD client, naming its document). It writes nothing and needs only clients.read.

Lifts the client's suspension, and switches on a client no developer owns; a developer's own switch stays theirs. Lifting a suspension also revokes any refresh token and spends any authorization code of the client left from before it (one a suspension by hand did not reach, say), so it brings none of them back. A security operation: the client obtains tokens again, so it needs clients.security and an approval, filed against the client as it stands; If-Match names its ETag (428 without it, 412 when it moved). It takes no body, or an empty object. A client already enabled is answered as it is.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

post.description: Suspends the client: it obtains no token until clients.enable lifts the suspension, and its owner cannot lift it. The suspension revokes every refresh token the client holds and spends its unredeemed authorization codes, so lifting it brings none of them back; for a service account's client, it also ends every admin token the service account holds. A write, which only takes tokens away, needing clients.write and no approval; for a client that holds an admin scope (qauth:admin:*), a security operation, needing clients.security and an approval, since no new admin token is issued through it once it is suspended. If-Match names its ETag (428 without it, 412 when it moved). It takes no body, or an empty object. A client already suspended is answered as it is.

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

get.summary: List the resource servers of a realm
get.description: Every resource server (protected resource, RFC 8707 and RFC 9728) the realm registers, newest first, one page at a time, each with the scopes it defines, their consent texts by locale and who may ask for them.

post.description: Registers a resource server: its resource indicator (an absolute URI with no fragment, never a QAuth API audience), the scopes it defines, each with its consent text by BCP 47 locale (en always among them) and whether it is sensitive, and who may ask for them, any_client or a list of client_ids. Each scope is then granted only when an authorization request names this resource, to a client it is open to, whatever the client’s own scopes list. A security operation: it needs resourceServers.security and an approval, filed with approvals.create for this body; a registration an approver could not be shown in full is refused (400). An indicator the realm already registered is 409.

get.description: The ETag is the version of the resource server: an update and a deletion name it in If-Match.

patch.description: A JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) of the resource server: scopes and clients, when named, replace the stored value whole; null removes neither (422). The resource indicator never changes (422): register another resource server for another one. Every change is a security operation, a narrowing too: it needs resourceServers.security and an approval, and a change an approver could not be shown in full is refused (422). If-Match names the ETag of the resource server (428 without it, 412 when it moved).

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

delete.description: Deletes the resource server: its scopes are no longer bound to its resource, so one no other resource server defines is granted again only to a client whose own scopes list it. Tokens already issued keep what they carry until they expire; a refresh that still carries one of its scopes is refused (invalid_scope) unless the client's own scopes list it. A security operation: it needs resourceServers.security and an approval, filed against the resource server as it stands; If-Match names its ETag (428 without it, 412 when it moved).

parameters.name: if-match
parameters.description: The ETag of the representation this update replaces (RFC 9110 §13.1.1).

post.summary: Preview a change of a resource server
post.description: Takes the JSON Merge Patch resourceServers.update takes and answers what it would change and need, without saving it: the scopes and who may ask for them, each before and after, tightening, loosening or neutral; for the whole patch, its class and scopes, that it needs an approval, whether a second admin is recommended or mandatory, how many other admins could approve it, and the resource server’s current ETag, which the save names in If-Match. It is refused as the save is (400, 415, 422). It writes nothing and needs only resourceServers.read.

post.summary: Plan the import of a realm file
post.description: A dry run: answers every change importing the file would make to the realm's policies and to the clients the operator manages, without applying it. Each change names its section, its item (a client's client_id) and its field, the value before and after, whether it tightens, loosens or neither (an unknown direction counts as loosening), and the class, effects, permissions and scopes of the single operation it equals: a policy change as realms.policies.update judges it, a client's field as clients.update does, and creating or deleting a client is a security change, as clients.create and clients.delete are. The plan's class is the strictest of its changes, and its digest, over the realm, the base policies version, the prune flag and the changes, is what the approval of the import binds to. A client the file leaves out stays unless prune is true. secretsToSet names the secrets the file's choices need and the realm lacks, such as mail.smtp.password once the file selects smtp: they are set on the realm, never by an import. A file the format refuses (422, each member at fault under /file), one holding a section this release does not import (cimd_clients, resources, system_client), one naming a client no realm file manages (a developer's, a self-registered or CIMD client, the system client, a service account's), and one that would create a client under the system client's client_id or a CIMD client_id are refused. It needs realms.import.plan, and realms.read and clients.read, since the plan shows the realm's policies and clients as they stand; it applies nothing and shows no secret. A realm with more than 10000 clients is refused (422).

dpopAuth.description: A DPoP-bound admin access token (RFC 9449 §7.1): `Authorization: DPoP <token>`, and a `DPoP` header holding a proof signed with the key the token names in `cnf.jkt`, for the request's method, ADMIN_API_BASE_URL followed by the request's path, an `iat` within 60 seconds, the token's hash as `ath` and a `jti` never used before. A Bearer token is refused.

mode.description: dry-run: answer the plan and apply nothing. The only mode this release takes; applying an import comes later (#531).

prune.description: Whether an item the realm has and the file leaves out is deleted. Left out: false, and nothing is deleted.

file.description: The realm file, as JSON: format urn:qauth:realm-file:v1-rc.0, whose JSON Schema is https://docs.qauth.dev/schemas/realm-file-v1-rc.0.json. A file the format refuses is answered 422, naming each member at fault.

kid.description: The provider's id of the key, kept as its kid, such as the Key ID Apple shows for a Sign in with Apple key.

sealed.description: The value, encrypted by secrets.seal for this member of this operation in the realm.

privateKey.description: The private key, unencrypted PKCS#8 or SEC 1 PEM (the contents of the .p8 file Apple issues), sealed by secrets.seal for plugins.keys.import, the member /privateKey and the params { plugin }.

kid.description: The plugin's next key, which signs its client assertions from now on.

AdminResourceServerDeleteRequestInput.description: No body, or an empty object.

AdminAccountDeletionRequestInput.description: No body, or an empty object.

accessTokenLifespanSeconds.description: How long an access token for a staging or production client is valid, in seconds, at most 86400 (a day). null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

developmentAccessTokenLifespanSeconds.description: How long an access token for a development client is valid, in seconds, at most 86400 (a day); no staging or production client receives it. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

refreshTokenLifespanSeconds.description: How long a refresh token is valid, in seconds, at most 7776000 (90 days), from its issue; a browser-based client's rotated token (a public client with an `https` redirect URI) never outlives the one it replaces, so its family ends with its first (RFC 10017). null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

adminAccessTokenLifespanSeconds.description: How long an access token for the admin API is valid, in seconds, at most 900, so a token whose audience is the admin API never lives longer, whatever the other lifetimes say (ADR-019 Decision 7: admin tokens are short-lived). null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

requireVerifiedAccount.description: Whether the legacy login routes (`POST /auth/login`, `POST /ui/login`) refuse an unverified account's right password with the answer a wrong password gets; the Interaction API verifies such an account inline with an emailed code, whatever this says. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

allowSignUp.description: Whether a person may create a new account through the hosted sign-in, from an unknown upstream identity (#639) or with `prompt=create` (#640, for a client whose `hosted_flows` name `register`), or through the legacy `POST /auth/register` (since 0.2.1; it answers 403 while this is off). null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

newFactorWindowDays.description: How many days, 0 to 30, a passkey or authenticator app bound after a sign-in that proved only the password stays new: the password alone may remove it, and it does not count as the account's strongest factor for a reset or a change; 0 means no window. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

minLength.description: The fewest characters (Unicode code points, after NFC normalisation) a new password may have, from 8 to 64; below 15 is a recorded deviation from NIST SP 800-63B-4 while a password can be the only factor. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

minScore.description: The lowest zxcvbn strength score, from 0 to 4, a new password may have. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

breachListSource.description: Which breach list new and presented passwords are checked against: off (the default), a list the operator supplies, or a k-anonymity range lookup through the egress client that sends only the first five hex characters of the password's SHA-1; a failed check never blocks a sign-in. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

enabled.description: Whether repeated failed sign-ins for one identifier lock it out for a while; when off, failures are only logged. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

maxAttempts.description: How many failed sign-ins within the window lock an identifier out. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

windowSeconds.description: The window, in seconds, over which failed sign-ins are counted, at most 86400 (a day). null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

lockoutSeconds.description: How long, in seconds, a locked-out identifier is refused before any password check, at most 86400 (a day). null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

requiredAtSignUp.description: Whether every `prompt=create` registration passes the bot challenge before its address is asked for, whatever the client; it then needs JavaScript, a client that cannot serve the challenge cannot register, and the legacy `POST /auth/register` ignores it. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

difficulty.description: How many leading zero bits the built-in proof of work asks for; each one doubles the work of the page that solves it, and 18 takes a browser a second or two. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

offerAfterSignIn.description: Whether the hosted sign-in offers to add a passkey after a password sign-in, to a verified account whose only factor is that password, while passkeys are on (`WEBAUTHN_ENABLED`); a passkey added from the account page is not affected. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

errorPage.description: The path on the realm origin, under `/ui/`, of the ceremony app’s page for the endings that leave no interaction to show (a provider callback whose sign-in has ended, the logout’s own pages), or null to keep the auth server’s own pages. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

dynamicRegistrationAllowedScopes.description: The scopes a dynamically registered client may hold; a scope outside the list is dropped from the registration, and no scope of the reserved qauth: namespace can be listed. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

enabled.description: Whether an HTTPS URL is accepted as a client_id, its metadata fetched from that URL (Client ID Metadata Documents). null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

trustPolicy.description: Which hosts a metadata-document client_id may have: any HTTPS host, or only the trusted domains. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

trustedDomains.description: The hosts the allowlist policy accepts, stored in lower case; an entry `*.example.com` accepts every subdomain of `example.com` but not `example.com` itself. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

provider.description: Which transport sends the realm mail: mock (logs only), resend or smtp. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

fromAddress.description: The address the realm mail is sent from. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

fromName.description: The sender name the realm mail shows. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

host.description: The SMTP server the smtp transport connects to. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

port.description: The port of the SMTP server. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

secure.description: Whether the SMTP connection uses TLS from its start. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

user.description: The user name the smtp transport signs in with. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

password.description: The password the smtp transport signs in with. A value sealed with secrets.seal for realms.policies.update and this member sets it, null clears it, leaving it out keeps it.

sealed.description: The value, encrypted by secrets.seal for this member of this operation in the realm.

anyOf.description: A secret, sealed with secrets.seal for this member of this operation in the realm: never the value itself.

passwordSet.description: Whether mail.smtp.password is set, as the representation shows it; it sets and clears nothing.

apiKey.description: The API key the resend transport sends with. A value sealed with secrets.seal for realms.policies.update and this member sets it, null clears it, leaving it out keeps it.

sealed.description: The value, encrypted by secrets.seal for this member of this operation in the realm.

anyOf.description: A secret, sealed with secrets.seal for this member of this operation in the realm: never the value itself.

apiKeySet.description: Whether mail.resend.apiKey is set, as the representation shows it; it sets and clears nothing.

verificationTokenExpirySeconds.description: How long a verification link is valid, in seconds, at least one hour. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

invalidateExistingTokensOnResend.description: Whether sending a new verification link makes the earlier ones invalid, so only the latest works. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

maxEnvironmentLaxity.description: The laxest environment profile a client of the realm may get; a client set to a laxer one gets this one. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

twoAdminMandatoryOperations.description: The admin operations that need a second admin approval in this realm, by operation id. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

workloadIssuers.description: The CI issuers whose workload tokens the operator realm exchanges for a service account admin token, with the audience, subject and service account of each. null gives it its default; the merged value is checked against the policy schema (422).

AdminClientDeleteRequestInput.description: No body, or an empty object.

AdminClientEnableRequestInput.description: No body, or an empty object.

AdminClientDisableRequestInput.description: No body, or an empty object.

type.description: The problem type: `https://docs.qauth.dev/reference/problem-types/#` followed by the type's slug.

reasons.description: For `weak_password`: why the new password was refused, in the order checked. A later release may add reasons.

max_age.description: For `insufficient_user_authentication`: the `max_age` of the challenge (RFC 9470 §3), in seconds. Send the person to the authorization endpoint with it, then repeat the call.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Branch on `code`, never on `title` or `detail`. `trace_id` is the id the server logged the request under. `errors` lists each field the request got wrong. `reasons` lists why a new password was refused (`weak_password`). `max_age` says how fresh the next sign-in must be (`insufficient_user_authentication`).

id.description: The id the admin API names the client by.

client_id.description: The OAuth client_id. For a client registered from a Client ID Metadata Document, the URL of that document.

developerId.description: The developer account that owns the client, or null: an operator registered it, an admin did, it registered itself, or its owner was deleted. Read-only.

provisionedByOperator.description: Whether an operator provisioned the client (the seed manifest, the system client, the admin API): only such a client takes a verified domain, and its authorization errors are redirected. Read-only.

dynamicallyRegistered.description: Whether the client registered itself (RFC 7591). Read-only.

metadataDocument.description: The Client ID Metadata Document the client’s settings come from, or null. A client with one is read-only here: its document is where it is changed (ADR-012 Decision 3). Read-only.

enabled.description: The owner’s switch. clients.enable turns it on for a client no developer owns. Read-only here.

suspended.description: Whether an operator suspended the client: it obtains no token until clients.enable lifts the suspension. Read-only here.

backchannelLogoutUriSource.description: Who set the back-channel logout URI: client, its own registration or document; admin, an operator or an admin, whose URI the deployment egress allowlist may let reach a private address. Read-only.

clientCredentialsScopes.description: The scopes the client_credentials grant may issue, out of scopes; null for any of them.

jwks.description: The public keys of a private_key_jwt client, inline; public members only.

dpopBoundAccessTokens.description: Whether every access token of the client is bound to a DPoP key (RFC 9449).

environment.description: The environment the client declares (ADR-008); the realm’s ceiling may make it stricter.

verifiedDomain.description: The domain an operator verified for the client (ADR-019 Decision 6), which every screen that names the client shows first.

firstPartyProfile.description: The first-party profile an operator set (ADR-017 Decision 2), or null when the client is not first party.

firstPartyPolicy.description: A native_backend client’s policy; null for any other.

firstPartyReason.description: The written reason for the first-party profile, exactly with one.

accessTokenLifespanSeconds.description: The client’s own access token lifetime, never longer than the realm’s; null for the realm’s. The token endpoint takes the shorter of the two.

refreshTokenLifespanSeconds.description: The client’s own refresh token lifetime, never longer than the realm’s; null for the realm’s.

lastUsedAt.description: When the client last obtained a token. Not part of the ETag.

scope.description: The scope value a client asks for.

text.description: The consent text the consent step shows for the scope, by BCP 47 locale; en is always among them, and shown when no other locale matches.

sensitive.description: Whether the realm flags the scope as sensitive: the consent step marks it.

id.description: The id the admin API names the resource server by.

resource.description: The resource indicator (RFC 8707): an absolute URI, matched exactly against the resource of an authorization request. It never changes: a new indicator is a new resource server.

scopes.description: The scopes the resource defines. Each is granted only when the authorization request names this resource, to a client the resource is open to, and with the user’s consent.

clients.description: Who may ask for the scopes: any_client, every client of the realm (CIMD and dynamically registered ones included), or the client_ids listed.

version.description: Raised by one with every change: the resource server’s ETag.

path.description: The dotted path of the field, such as password.minScore.

before.description: The stored value; for a secret field, set or not set, never a value.

after.description: The value the save would store; for a secret field, set or not set, never a value.

direction.description: Whether the change tightens, loosens or neither; a change whose direction is unknown counts as loosening.

class.description: security when this change needs qauth:admin:security and an approval.

effects.description: The effects that make this change a security change; empty for a write.

permissions.description: The admin permissions this change needs.

scopes.description: The admin scopes this change needs.

secret.description: Whether the field is a secret, shown only as set or not set.

environmentBound.description: Whether the value describes the environment the realm runs in, which a sandbox promotion leaves out unless it is selected (ADR-019 Decision 11).

etag.description: The ETag of the resource as the preview read it: the save names it in If-Match, and is refused with 412 once the resource has moved on.

class.description: The strictest class of the save: security when any change is, or the save cannot be classified.

effects.description: Every effect of the save’s security changes.

permissions.description: Every admin permission the save needs, reading what it answers included.

scopes.description: Every admin scope the save needs.

approvalRequired.description: Whether the save runs only with an approval: exactly when it is a security save.

twoAdmin.description: Whether a second admin’s approval is recommended or mandatory for the save; null when it needs no approval.

eligibleApprovers.description: How many admins other than the caller hold the right to approve the save on the realm: those a second admin’s approval could come from: every admin with a grant on the realm, and, for a caller of the operator realm, every admin with a grant on every realm, which no other realm sees. 0 when the caller is the only one; null when the save needs no approval. Today an approval takes the caller’s own step-up alone, and a second admin’s is recommended.

changes.description: Every field the save changes, in the order of the schema; empty when none.

refreshTokenLifespanSeconds.description: The client’s own refresh token lifetime, never longer than the realm’s; null for the realm’s.

clientSecret.description: The client secret of a client that authenticates with one, answered here once and never again. Absent for private_key_jwt and none.

section.description: The section of the realm file: policies or clients.

key.description: The item's natural key, such as a client's client_id; null for the policies, whose fields are matched by their path.

path.description: The dotted path of the field within the item, such as password.minScore or redirect_uris; empty when the change creates or deletes the whole item.

op.description: create for an item the realm lacks, update for a field of one it has, delete for an item it has and the file leaves out, which only a pruning import deletes.

before.description: The value the realm holds, as stored; null for an item it lacks. A secret field shows set or not set, never a value.

after.description: The value the import would store; null for an item it deletes. A secret field shows set or not set, never a value.

direction.description: Whether the change tightens, loosens or neither; a change whose direction is unknown counts as loosening.

needsSecret.description: Whether the change leaves the realm needing a secret it does not hold: one secretsToSet names, or the client secret of a client that authenticates with one.

baseVersion.description: The realm's policies_version the plan was made against: the realm's ETag, without its quotes.

prune.description: Whether items the realm has and the file leaves out are deleted.

digest.description: The SHA-256 digest, base64url, of the RFC 8785 form of the realm id, the base version, the prune flag and the changes as the plan shows them, a URL credential masked: the approval of the import binds to it, and the apply refuses a plan whose digest differs.

class.description: The strictest class of the changes: security when any change is; write when none is, or when there is no change.

effects.description: Every effect of the security changes.

permissions.description: Every admin permission the changes need; empty when there is no change.

scopes.description: Every admin scope the changes need.

approvalRequired.description: Whether applying the plan needs an approval: exactly when it is security.

secretsToSet.description: The secret fields the file's choices need and the realm lacks, by path, such as mail.smtp.password: set on the realm itself, never by an import.

warnings.description: What the import does not stop on but says, such as a file written for a realm of another name.

changes.description: Every change, section by section in the order of the realm file, each section in its own order; empty when the file matches the realm.

algorithm.description: The key's JWS algorithm: the one the plugin's configuration asks for.

status.description: active: it signs the plugin's client assertions now. next: it waits for plugins.keys.activate, and the active key signs until then.

activatedKid.description: The key that signs from now on.

retiredKid.description: The key that stopped signing, or null when the plugin had no active key.

operator.description: Whether this is the operator realm, whose admins may hold grants on other realms.

sandbox.description: This realm's sandbox, or null. Read-only.

verifiedAt.description: When the operator verified the account.

method.description: How it was verified: operator, an admin's approved users.verify; operator_cli, the verify-account command on the server host. The set may grow.

verifiedBy.description: Who verified it: the admin account for operator, the operating-system user for operator_cli, or null when the host named none.
